basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 21.' and it opens 'Vers. 21. Pactum meum statuam cum Isaac. Quia misericordia et gratia ejus in populo est'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text:
Vers. 21. Pactum meum statuam cum Isaac. Quia misericordia et gratia ejus in populo est Christiano.

Vers 23. Circumcidit Ismaelem et cunctos mares. Quaeri potest, si mares circumcisione salvabantur, feminae quomodo salvabantur, quae non circumcidebantur? Utique fide et hostiarum oblatione, quomodo et per ante dictum praeceptum circumcisionis sancti homines mundabantur, juxta quod Paulus | dicit: fide purificans corda (Act. X, 9).
